newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Market dull in pre-weekend mood.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Market dull in pre-weekend mood.

text.p: Talk was thin and prices hardly changed in the Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market on Friday despite strength in the swaps market, traders said.
The cargo market was bathed in a pre-weekend mood and many players took a wait-and-see attitude, searching for a fresh market direction to follow.
Helped by overnight gains in crude values, July swaps edged up to $99.75/$100.50 from Thursday's $99.00/$99.75 and August swaps advanced to $99.25/$100.00 against $98.75/$99.50.
Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) said it had awarded two 30,000-tonne, 180-cst cargoes at around $100.50 per tonne for lifting in the first half of July.
Overall sentiment was sluggish although traders were expecting supplies to start tightening, which should support prices in the near term.
Kuwait is reducing its exports during the summer season when its domestic need for air-conditioning rises, while some South Korean refineries are still shut or maintenance.
"There is only routine demand from some countries such as Taiwan and South Korea. There is no fresh demand," said one trader.
Taiwan's CPC has an outstanding tender to buy at least one 38,000-tonne cargo of 0.5-percent sulphur fuel oil for delivery between July 21 and August 15.
The tender will close on June 18 and offers will be valid for two days.
The Korean Electric Power Company (KEPCO) also tendered to buy three 74,000-tonne cargoes of 0.3-percent, 540-cst fuel oil for August and September deliveries.
The tender will close on June 19 and offers will be valid for three days.
